headline: Police baton-charge HSC students demanding Education Minister's resignation
summary: Protesters gathered in front of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban to oppose the decision to hold exams during severe flooding and waterlogging.
details: Police baton-charged HSC examinees who gathered in front of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban on Tuesday evening, demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon.
The clash occurred around 6:30 PM after protesters refused to leave the parliament complex despite repeated requests from law enforcement officers.
Earlier in the afternoon, students also blocked the Science Lab intersection to reiterate their demands for the minister's resignation.
The demonstrators are opposing the government's decision to conduct HSC and equivalent examinations amidst severe flooding and waterlogging in various parts of the country.
Students have also raised concerns over alleged errors in question papers and criticized remarks reportedly made by the minister regarding the examinees.
Protesters accused the government of ignoring the hardships faced by students affected by heavy rainfall and floods, vowing to continue their movement.
However, Inspector (Investigation) Azizur Rahaman of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station denied the use of batons, stating that students left the area on their own.
caption:
Police clash with HSC students in front of Parliament. Protesters are demanding the Education Minister's resignation over flood-hit exam schedules.

Police baton-charged HSC examinees who gathered in front of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban on Tuesday evening, demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon.

The clash occurred around 6:30 PM after protesters refused to leave the parliament complex despite repeated requests from law enforcement officers.

Earlier in the afternoon, students also blocked the Science Lab intersection to reiterate their demands for the minister's resignation.

The demonstrators are opposing the government's decision to conduct HSC and equivalent examinations amidst severe flooding and waterlogging in various parts of the country.

Students have also raised concerns over alleged errors in question papers and criticized remarks reportedly made by the minister regarding the examinees.

Protesters accused the government of ignoring the hardships faced by students affected by heavy rainfall and floods, vowing to continue their movement.

However, Inspector (Investigation) Azizur Rahaman of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station denied the use of batons, stating that students left the area on their own.

headline: 1 in 13 Bangladeshi women experience early menopause, study finds
summary: A major multi-country study led by icddr,b reveals that 7.5% of women in Bangladesh enter menopause before age 45, linked to education and rural living.
details: Around one in every 13 Bangladeshi women experiences menopause before the age of 45, according to a large multi-country study led by researchers at icddr,b.
The study, published in BMJ Global Health, found a prevalence of 7.5% in Bangladesh, which is slightly above the average of 7.1% for low- and middle-income countries.
Early menopause occurs before age 45, while premature menopause occurs before age 40. Women who experience this lose the protective effects of oestrogen earlier than expected.
Global evidence indicates that early menopause is linked to a higher lifetime risk of cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, cognitive decline, and depression.
The research found that women in rural areas were 17% more likely to experience early menopause than those in urban areas, pointing to inequalities in healthcare and nutrition.
Education was a strong protective factor: women with higher education had 58% lower odds of early menopause compared to those with no formal education.
Other risk factors included marrying or having a first child before the age of 18, which significantly increased the likelihood of early menopause.
Researchers call for greater investment in girls' education, efforts to prevent child marriage, and the integration of menopause history into routine healthcare.
